text:
Enjoy today, because it's the last mild one for a while. It's mostly cloudy with a high near 64, and a spotty shower is possible, though most of the day stays dry. Tonight cools to around 45, with a few sprinkles possible toward dawn.

Saturday is where the pattern flips. A slow-moving low settles in, and the high only gets to about 54, with some of the models closer to 50. Rain is likely all day, but the morning is light, under a tenth of an inch. The steadier rain arrives around lunchtime and peaks from about 2 to 4 in the afternoon, so do your errands early and keep the umbrella close after noon. Saturday night is the soaker, a quarter to half inch, with a low near 37. The latest guidance has trended wetter for us, so a bigger total, even up to an inch, isn't off the table if the low strengthens quickly. A little wet snow may mix in on the highest hills overnight, but I'd expect plain rain down here.

Sunday starts wet, with rain tapering off around 1, then a few leftover showers and a brief break. It stays mostly cloudy. The forecasters say 52 for the high, but the models lean cooler, so I'd bet on the upper 40s to low 50s. Showers return Sunday night, and next week looks chilly. Sunday afternoon is your best window for a walk.
